title: dont type number
rule: Do not use `type="number"` on Text Field — allows `e`/`+`/`-`/`.` and silently discards others; scroll increment is accidental. MUI points at GOV.UK number inputs. Dual-cite; do not invent a winner vs Apple number formatter. Fail native `type=number`. Formatted numeric control is Apple's claim, not a house pick.
pass_when: The Text Field does not use native `type="number"`. A formatted numeric control may exist as Apple's claim — not required or banned here.
overview: Do not use native type=number on Text Field; it allows e/+/-/. and accidental scroll increment.
apply_when: Collecting numeric values in an MUI Text Field.
not_when: Not for non-numeric text, or separate formatted numeric controls claimed elsewhere.
agent_hint: Avoid native type=number on Text Field; do not rely on its silent filtering.
description: Do not put native `type="number"` on a Text Field: it allows `e`, `+`, `-`, and `.`, silently drops other characters, and makes scroll increment accidental. Those behaviors create surprising invalid or discarded input. Fail whenever the Text Field uses native `type="number"`. A formatted numeric control may exist as another claim—it is neither required nor banned here. Apply when collecting numeric values in an MUI Text Field.
do_not_claim: A house winner vs Apple number formatter; that formatted numeric entry is forbidden.
